title: Mixed-precision kernel selection and dequant path minimization for INT8/FP8 inference
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead when serving quantized INT8/FP8 model variants by selecting kernels that avoid repeated dequant -> compute -> requant cycles, and by scheduling prefill/decode work so dequantization is batched and fused where possible.

Background: We have two related sources of overhead for quantized paths: (1) control-path and memory-copy costs introduced by switching between quantized kernel implementations and FP compute kernels, and (2) runtime dequant/requant operations performed at attention and FFN boundaries. On workloads with short decode latencies and small batch sizes, these overheads dominate token cost and p50 latency.

Scope: This ticket covers kernel selection heuristics in the serving runtime and small kernel changes to support fused dequant+matmul and mixed-precision attention. It does not include end-to-end quantization tooling or model recalibration (separate tickets). Deliverables: a kernel-selection decision table, runtime heuristics to pick fused paths, microbenchmarks demonstrating dequant overhead reduction, and a canary rollout plan for runtime-2.4.

High-level approach:
- Add a "quantized-fused" kernel family that takes int8/uint8 or fp8 inputs and performs dequant + matmul + optional activation in a single GPU kernel where memory formats align.
- Extend kernel registry with tags: precision_hint (INT8/FP8/FP16), supports_fused_dequant (yes/no), preferred_alignment (bytes), fallback_cost_estimate (ns).
- At request scheduling time use a lightweight cost model (based on sequence length, batch size, cached KV presence, and precision_hint) to prefer fused kernels for prefill and first-k decode tokens.
- For decode scheduling, group streams by sequence-length bucket and precision to increase chances of continuous fused execution and reduce kernel churn.
- Where fusion is impossible, prefer mixed-precision kernels that keep accumulation in FP16/FP32 while consuming quantized weights, minimizing dequant passes to one per layer.

Non-goals / out of scope:
- Full quantization-aware training or calibration flows.
- Large refactors of kernel internals beyond enabling a small fused wrapper.

Acceptance criteria (see list): ensure measurable perf and correct outputs for a small set of models before canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end generation latency (prefill + 1 decode token) reduced by at least 18% p50 on small-batch INT8 path compared to baseline with separate dequant kernels.
Per-token GPU time for attention+FFN layers shows >= 20% decrease in dequant-related memory copies for fused kernel paths in microbenchmarks.

Runtime selects fused or mixed-precision kernel deterministically for the same request fingerprint (sequence length, batch size, model precision), and falls back to compatible path when fused kernel not available.
Numerical equivalence: fused/mixed paths differ from reference FP16 run by no more than 1e-3 average logit-scale across a 100-sample eval prompt set used by runtime-performance QA.
Unit and integration tests for kernel registry tags, scheduler heuristics, and a small GPU smoke test are added and passing in CI.
Canary rollout plan documented and validated: canary on dedicated GPUs with traffic split and automatic rollback on error or latency regressions >10%.
Benchmarks and a cost analysis report are uploaded to Confluence and linked in the ticket.
tech_notes: Kernel registry extension: add 'precision_hint' and 'supports_fused_dequant' fields; keep registry lookup O(1) via hashed tag vector.
Fused kernel prototype implemented as a thin wrapper calling cuBLASGEMM with pre-dequant step fused into kernel when weights are pretransposed and stored in block-int8 format.
Mixed-precision attention: use int8 weights with fp16 accumulation and optional fp32 reduction for final softmax to preserve dynamic range on long sequences.
Dequant strategy: avoid per-request dequant copies by exposing a shared dequant buffer for a worker and reference-counting pinned pages when multiple streams can reuse layout.

Scheduler heuristics: cost_estimate = alpha * seq_len + beta * decode_flag + gamma / batch_size + delta * (supports_fused ? 0 : 1). Alpha/beta/gamma/delta tunable via runtime flags and autotuning job.
Benchmarks: initial microbench uses Llama-2-13B quantized INT8 (GPTQ-style) and an FP8 variant; measured on A100 80GB with sequence lengths {16,64,256} and batch sizes {1,4,8}.

Preliminary numbers (internal microbench): small-batch prefill p50 improved 22% when fused; decode token p50 improved 12% due to kernel churn remaining for short decodes — improvement target unmet for some decode shapes.
Confluence: /docs/runtime/kernel-fusion-dequant (design doc) contains detailed memory layout diagrams and fallback decision matrix.
Compatibility: add runtime flag --quant-kernel-mode with options {auto, prefer-fused, prefer-fallback} for A/B testing; default 'auto'.
